steps: Wash the apples to remove obvious dirt, and cut out any bruised or bird-struck bits.
Crush the apples, or put them through a juice maker, and collect the juice in one of the fermenters.
Cover the fermenter with a cloth, or plug the opening with cotton wool if narrow, to keep out dust and insects. Do not fill completely: air space brings oxygen to vinegar bacteria.
Set aside to ferment at about 18–22°C (64–72°F). It should bubble within a couple of days. Note progress to identify when fermentation peaks and slows.
When fermentation slows, siphon carefully into the other fermenter, avoiding sediment and froth—the aim is clear cider without floating chunks.
Set the second fermenter aside for two to three months. A white film on top is the vinegar mother formed by acetobacter.
After a couple of months draw off two thirds of the vinegar for use, and top up with fresh clear cider made in the first fermenter.
